title: Numeric search filters must bind ints on SQL stores (psycopg v3 VARCHAR bind)
answers: PostgreSQL search fails with 'operator does not exist: bigint > character varying' when filtering experiments, datasets or model versions by time or version number
numeric filter on creation_time or created_time errors under psycopg v3 or SQLAlchemy 2.1
searching model versions by version_number fails on postgresql+psycopg
why do time-based search filters break only on PostgreSQL with psycopg3
body:
Symptom: On PostgreSQL with psycopg v3 (SQLAlchemy 2.1 default or postgresql+psycopg), time and version_number search filters fail with 'operator does not exist: bigint > character varying'.
Root cause: mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:_get_search_experiments_filter_clauses and _get_search_datasets_filter_clauses, and mlflow/store/model_registry/sqlalchemy_store.py:_get_search_model_versions_filter_clauses, passed the parsed filter string straight into SearchUtils.get_sql_comparison_func. psycopg v3 binds str as VARCHAR, which PostgreSQL will not compare to an integer column.
Fix pattern: after the comparator is validated, coerce the numeric attribute with int(value) inside try/except (TypeError, ValueError) and re-raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value with "Invalid value for numeric attribute '<key>': <repr>". Do this for every integer column touched by a search, including experiment_id-style lookups where the bound value is a str such as store.DEFAULT_EXPERIMENT_ID (tests bind int(...) there).
Constraints: Applies to SQL-backed stores only. Validate the comparator before coercing. Do not coerce string attributes such as name or run_id.
applies: SQLAlchemy tracking and model-registry store search filter builders for integer columns (experiment times, dataset times, model version_number).
says: Filtering experiments or datasets by creation time fails on PostgreSQL with a type error.
Searching model versions by version number crashes when connected to a Postgres database.
Allow numeric comparisons on model version numbers in the model registry search bar.
Dataset time filter queries fail because the database rejects comparing numbers to text.
search: SQL store search filter builders in mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py and mlflow/store/model_registry/sqlalchemy_store.py must coerce numeric attribute values with int(value) after validating the comparator. Without coercion, psycopg v3 binds strings as VARCHAR, causing PostgreSQL to fail with 'operator does not exist: bigint > character varying' when comparing against integer columns such as time or version_number. The conversion must catch TypeError and ValueError and re-raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value, applying to every integer column touched by search including experiment_id lookups. This rule applies exclusively to SQL-backed stores, requires validating comparators first, and must not coerce string attributes such as name or run_id.
